cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has a new message: the burden against Egypt. The LORD rides on a swift cloud, and He is coming to Egypt. Meanwhile it takes me three hops on this gold base just to cross my own bakery.

cards.question: The LORD is coming to Egypt on a swift cloud. What happens to the idols of Egypt?

answers.text: They are carried off to Babylon
They are hidden in the temples

cards.question: The LORD rides into Egypt on a swift cloud, and the hearts of the Egyptians will ___ within them.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: He'll stir up Egyptian against Egyptian, brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city. My six kids once fought over a single chocolate chip, and that was just ONE counter.

cards.question: Egypt is fighting itself, and the LORD frustrates their plans. Who do the Egyptians turn to?

answers.text: Idols and spirits of the dead

cards.question: The Lord GOD of Hosts declares He will deliver the Egyptians into the hands of a ___ master.

cards.text: Now the message turns to the Nile, Egypt's great river.

cards.question: In this message against Egypt, what happens to the waters of the Nile?

cards.text: And it spreads: the canals stink, the reeds wither, and the fields along the Nile blow away. That's like trying to bake with no dough, friend. You're just standing there holding a stamper.

cards.question: With the Nile drying up, the fishermen of Egypt celebrate.

cards.text: The flax workers are dismayed, the linen weavers turn pale, and all the hired workers are sick at heart. That's a whole lot of folks staring at a riverbed like it owes them money.

The princes of Zoan are mere fools, and Pharaoh's counselors give senseless advice while saying, 'I am one of the wise, a son of eastern kings.' That's me in my blurry years telling Mother Miller, 'Trust me, I'm a professional.'

cards.question: Pharaoh's counselors claim to be wise. So the message asks where those wise men are now. What does it dare them to do?

answers.text: Reveal what the LORD has planned
Bring the Nile back to life
Make peace with the land of Judah

cards.text: It gets worse. The princes of Memphis are deceived too, and Egypt staggers through all she does, as a drunkard staggers.

cards.question: Egypt's leaders are lost and the whole land is staggering. Where did this spirit of confusion come from?

answers.text: The LORD poured it into her
Her idols poured it into her

cards.question: By the end of all this, there is nothing Egypt can do, from the head to the tail.

cards.text: In that day, the Egyptians tremble with fear beneath the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, when He brandishes it against them.

cards.question: The land of ___ will bring terror to Egypt, and whenever it's mentioned, Egypt will tremble over what the LORD of Hosts has planned.

cards.text: Then, out of NOWHERE, the message turns: in that day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan. One of them will even be called the City of the Sun.

cards.question: Those five cities in Egypt swear allegiance to someone. Who is it?

cards.text: In that day there's an altar to the LORD right in the center of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD near her border. Same country, whole new centerpiece.

cards.question: When the Egyptians cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, He sends them a savior and defender to rescue them.
The LORD makes Himself known to Egypt. What does Egypt do on that day?

cards.text: They worship with sacrifices and offerings, and they make vows to the LORD and fulfill them. I once vowed to keep my apron spotless, and friend, do NOT ask my apron how that went.

cards.question: The LORD strikes Egypt with a plague and then leaves them to suffer.

cards.text: In that day there's a highway from Egypt to Assyria, with Assyrians heading to Egypt and Egyptians heading to Assyria. I bet it's the only traffic jam anybody's ever been happy to sit in.

cards.question: On that highway, the Egyptians and the Assyrians will ___ together.

cards.text: And in that day Israel joins them in a three-party alliance with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing upon the earth.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts blesses Egypt, Assyria and Israel. What does He call Egypt?

cards.text: Hear the whole blessing: 'Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.' Friend, I'm standing here on my gold base with my mustache over my mouth.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 mentions jam, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new moment in the Millers' kitchen: his six kids fighting over a chocolate chip. The backstory shows the kids lovingly, and this adds something new to it. The made-up moment happens on the Millers' counter, not around his bakery, so it isn't covered by the allowance for bakery moments. The punchline 'that was just ONE counter' also doesn't connect clearly to a nation fighting itself.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new backstory moment in the Millers' kitchen: Papa Dorin telling Mother Miller 'Trust me, I'm a professional' during his blurry years. Nothing in the backstory shows him talking to the Millers, and this moment isn't around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The card says the counselors give senseless advice 'while saying' they are wise. Verse 11 only asks, 'How can you say to Pharaoh…'. It doesn't tie the claim to the moment they give advice, so 'while' adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says 'Egypt staggers through all she does, as a drunkard staggers.' Verse 14 says Egypt 'has been led astray in all she does, as a drunkard staggers.' Staggering is the comparison, but the card makes it the plain action and drops 'led astray.' Card 15's question has the same problem ('the whole land is staggering').

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question calls it fact that 'the whole land is staggering.' In verse 14, staggering is only the drunkard comparison for Egypt being led astray.

No card ever tells the turn in verse 22: the LORD strikes Egypt but heals them, they turn to the LORD, and He hears their prayers. The only coverage is a true or false statement whose right answer is False. That tells the baker what doesn't happen, never what does. This is a key turn in the passage's second half.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question says the Egyptians and Assyrians worship together 'On that highway.' Verse 23 mentions the highway and then says they will worship together, but it never says the worship happens on the highway.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the exact title the LORD gives Egypt ('My people' against 'My servant' and 'My firstborn'). It is guessing a word-level detail of a line, like the anointing-oil example. No earlier card gives a basis for reasoning to 'My people' over 'My servant,' so it comes down to luck. A better question would ask about the meaning of the blessing, like Egypt and Assyria being blessed alongside Israel.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
